newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala calls state of alert as volcano erupts.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala calls state of alert as volcano erupts.

text.p: Emergency workers were on a state of alert on Friday after a volcano south of the Guatemalan capital erupted around midnight, setting off a two-hour string of explosions, authorities said.

"We are in constant radio communication (in case of) any strange behaviour by the volcano and to coordinate evacuation if necessary," Paul de Leon, spokesman at the National Emergency Committee, said.

The Pacaya volcano, 24 miles (40 kilometres) south of Guatemala City, erupted from midnight to two a.m., drawing fascinated residents of the capital from their beds to witness the fiery explosions and molten lava that flowed down the volcano's flanks.
The eruption caused no deaths or injuries and lava flows did not come near any villages, according to De Leon.

During the eruption, emergency workers were sent to evacuate hundreds of villages on the sides of the volcano, which is often climbed by tourists. They ended up moving less than a hundred people, and those were back in their homes by sunrise as fears abated, De Leon said.
The 8421-foot (2552-meter) Pacaya is one of several active volcanos studded across Guatemala, and it erupts regularly.
Eddy Sanchez, director of the National Seismological Institute said it was the biggest eruption at Pacaya since 1987.
